name: Insulin aspart
summary: A rapid-acting insulin analog for mealtime glucose coverage with fast subcutaneous absorption, available in pump-compatible and faster-acting formulations.
mechanism: Substituting proline with aspartic acid at position B28 reduces hexamer self-association, accelerating absorption after subcutaneous injection.
pharmacodynamics: Provides a rapid prandial insulin peak; used in basal-bolus regimens, pumps, and mixed with basal insulins in fixed-ratio products.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Enzymatic degradation (insulin-degrading enzymes); hepatic and renal clearance

dosing.adult: Individualized; typically given immediately before or within 20 minutes of starting a meal, as part of a basal-bolus or pump regimen

safety.pregnancy: Safe and standard; insulin is the preferred glucose-lowering treatment in pregnancy
safety.lactation: Generally safe; insulin does not cross into breast milk in significant amounts
safety.overdose: Hypoglycemia; treat with oral or IV glucose and close monitoring

clinicalPearls: Fiasp (faster aspart with niacinamide) has an even earlier onset for those needing quicker coverage.
Fixed-ratio combinations (e.g., aspart + degludec) simplify basal-bolus regimens.
good: Rapid, reliable prandial coverage with pump compatibility.
bad: Requires basal coverage; hypoglycemia if meals are delayed after injection.
